headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP surfaces make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default between ECC and OpenMetadata.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads/writes local files, uses MCP, and treats skills/hooks/configs as workflow surfaces; OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible bridge where OpenMetadata-originated content can reach ECC parsers or files without provenance tracking. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is routed into ECC files, hooks, or MCP inputs without provenance checks
IF ECC treats external file or MCP content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata outputs into ECC workflows
Require provenance tags on all MCP/file inputs before ECC parses them
Separate the two agents onto distinct workspaces
Review and strip instruction-like text from OpenMetadata exports before handoff
requires-engineering: add allowlisted schemas for inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, documentation, and security findings, and can write/read the filesystem. OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge and exposes APIs/webhooks/MCP. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive metadata can flow from ECC into OpenMetadata or vice versa; the docs do not show isolation, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted files
IF either agent forwards file contents or metadata to its backend or APIs
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory and mount
Restrict shared files to non-sensitive samples only
Rotate any shared API tokens used by either agent
Audit recent ECC session files for sensitive metadata
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Their write surfaces overlap on shared mutable resources, so concurrent edits or conflicting metadata updates are plausible. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, but the blast radius is usually recoverable, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repo, config tree, or metadata store
IF no external lock or transaction boundary is enforced
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource
Use separate branches or namespaces for concurrent work
Pause one agent while the other performs writes
Check in changes frequently to reduce merge conflicts
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking or optimistic concurrency

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces security findings, documentation, and code-related outputs, while OpenMetadata manages lineage, governance, and trust metadata through APIs and webhooks. If OpenMetadata consumes ECC output as authoritative, a mistaken finding or malformed metadata can cascade into downstream catalog updates or actions. The pairwise handoff is inferred, but the default integration surface is broad enough to justify high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests ECC outputs without human verification
IF ECC outputs are used to update lineage, governance, or trust records
mitigations: Require human review before OpenMetadata acts on ECC output
Compare ECC claims against source records before import
Limit ECC to draft-only outputs
Log and diff all metadata updates from the handoff
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported findings

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, but they do show different retention-sensitive data classes and API/webhook exposure. That is enough for a compliance mismatch risk in default deployments, though not a residency breach.
conditions: IF the same regulated dataset is stored in both agents with different retention rules
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs export data outside the approved jurisdiction
mitigations: Document retention rules for each agent
Exclude regulated fields from ECC session storage
Review OpenMetadata export and webhook destinations
Delete stale session artifacts on a fixed schedule
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
